newsitem.title: JAPAN: Small fire at TEPCO nuclear plant extinguished.
newsitem.headline: Small fire at TEPCO nuclear plant extinguished.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc said a small fire occured at its Kashiwazaki Kariwa nuclear plant on Wednesday morning, but was quickly extinguished.
The fire caused no radiation leakage and had no impact on operations at the plant, which is located about 220 km northwest of Tokyo, a TEPCO spokesman said.

Eyewitnesses said the fire occured at a toilet in a building housing the No. 3 reactor at 9.52 a.m. (0052 GMT) and was brought under control by plant workers with fire extinguishers, he said, adding that the local fire department confirmed the fire had been put out at 10.24 a.m. (0124 GMT).
"There was absolutely no radiation leakage or impact on the plant's operations," he said.
The 1.1 million kilowatt (kw) reactor has been shut since April 24 for routine maintenance checks, and the cause of the fire is under investigation, he said.
The spokesman also said the toilet is equipped with an electric heater to process human waste, and the heater could have caused the fire.

TEPCO on Tuesday closed another 1.1 million kw reactor at its Fukushima No.2 Nuclear Power Plant, about 100 km northwest of Tokyo, after the radioactivity level of exhaust gas went 20 times higher than normal late on Monday night.
The electric utility, which is currently investigating what caused the surge, said a pinhole in the metal cover of a nuclear fuel rod in the reactor could have caused the radiation leakage.
